newsitem.title: UK: Reed Intnl extends losses on downgrading.
newsitem.headline: Reed Intnl extends losses on downgrading.

text.p: Shares in Reed International Plc extended earlier sharp losses as brokerage houses downgraded profit forecasts after the company's meeting with analysts.
At 1615 GMT, Reed shares were down 65p at 10.86-1/2 stg after earlier trading as high as 11.89 stg. Volume was heavy at almost 11 million shares.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Richard Jolliffe said he was considering reducing his 1997 pretax profit forecast to 888 million stg, down 41 million from the previous figure.
He said this was based on the strength of sterling but there were also other fundamental factors depressing the share price. He declined to elaborate.

UBS analyst Colin Tennant said the company's trading statement on Thursday flagged that if exchange rates stayed where they were there would be a negative impact on 1997 earnings. "I think people are factoring that in," he said.
He said pretax profit figures could come out at about 860-880 million stg, down about five percent from his previous expectation.
UBS was recommending holding Reed shares. "But this is clearly negative news," Tennant said.
Earlier, market sources said HSBC James Capel had trimmed earnings estimates for Reed by some seven percent, though analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment.
